newsitem.title: HONG KONG: WEEKAHEAD - HK stocks seen up but vulnerable.
newsitem.headline: WEEKAHEAD - HK stocks seen up but vulnerable.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to regain some lost ground next week after U.S. jobs data failed to rattle Wall Street as some investors had feared, but prices were still vulnerable to interest rate jitters, analysts said.

The U.S. Labour Department said non-farm payrolls rose by 250,000 in August, slightly more than the 244,000 forecast by economists. The Dow industrials rose 52.90 points to 5,659.86 on Friday and the U.S. long bond added 17/32 to yield 7.11 percent.
"I think the reaction on Wall Street will help the recovery of local shares next week," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
Analysts said the data still pointed to a strong U.S. economy but gave investors hope that a possible near-term rate hike by the U.S. Federal Reserve would only be modest.
"If you look at the job numbers, the market expects quite a moderate rate hike. Market weakness in the recent week already reflects that concern," said Kwong.
The Hang Seng index fell 133.43 points, or 1.2 percent, last week. On Friday, it shed 14.92 points to close at 11,025.59.
"I think the market will rise steadily on selective buying," said Alex Tang, research director at Yamaichi International.
"There will be steady buying, especially from U.S. firms that sold last week," he said.
However, with the possibility of a near-term rate hike still hanging over the market, investors were likely to tread cautiously, analysts said. The Fed will meet on September 24.
"It is certainly not going to be full speed ahead," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities. He pointed to the U.S. long bond yield at 7.11 percent.
"The long bond is still doing a 7-11 on us so there is no real incentive for the market to do much," he said.
Rossiter said stocks could edge up on Monday but then ease back to 10,800-10,900 points later in the week.
"Investors are still not certain about the stability of Wall Street, and we still have more (economic) numbers coming out," added Kwong.
U.S. August producer prices are scheduled for release on Thursday and U.S. August consumer prices on Friday. "They may also be key figures," said Kwong.
He expected the Hang Seng index to trade in a range of 10,850 to 11,250 points, with corporate earnings and results of property sales possibly allowing the blue chip index to test the upper limit.
Henderson Land and Development Co Ltd, Henderson Investment Ltd and Henderson China Holdings Ltd are due to report fiscal 1996 results on Wednesday.

Analysts expect Henderson Land to report net profit of about HK$8.0 billion, up from HK$7.03 billion the previous year, and Henderson Investment to post fiscal 1996 earnings of about HK$2.2 billion compared with HK$1.63 billion.
Hong Kong & China Gas Co Ltd is scheduled to report its interim results on Tuesday.

Analysts said investors will also be looking closely at Swire Pacific Ltd's pre-sale of 48 residential units at Island Place. Swire said it will start the sale in the coming week at an average price of HK$6,282 per sq ft.
"Corporate results and property sales will help support the market," said Kwong.
